Lessons.Title: Graphs of Logarithmic Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: The parent y=log_b(x), b>0 and b!=1, has domain x>0, full real range, vertical asymptote x=0, and x-intercept(1,0).
For y=a·log_b(c(x−h))+k, solve the complete argument positivity constraint first; the asymptote is at the argument zero whenever c!=0.
Replacing x by −x reflects a logarithmic graph over the y-axis and changes its domain. A negative multiplier reflects over the x-axis.
Horizontal translations change logarithmic domains and vertical asymptotes; vertical translations do not change full real range.
Graphs of b^x and log_b(x) reflect across y=x; use independent points and graph reasoned features.
Before solving equations combining logarithms, restrict every argument to be strictly positive. Verify candidate roots in the original equations.
Independent Cool-down: (a) graph y=log_2(x−3), (b) give domain and asymptote of ln(5−x), (c) solve ln(x+1)=0.
Independent Try It 1: Find domain and asymptote of ln(x+3).
Independent Try It 2: Find domain and asymptote of ln(4−x).
Independent Try It 3: Give points for log_3(x).
Independent Try It 4: Shift y=log_2(x) right1.
Independent Try It 5: Shift y=ln(x) up3.
Independent Try It 6: Compress y=log_2(x) vertically by1/2.
Independent Try It 7: Graph y=3log_2(x−2)+1, give domain.
Independent Try It 8: Reflect y=ln(x) about y-axis.
Independent Try It 10: Find asymptote for log(7−x).
Independent Try It 11: Find equation of right shifted log_2 with asymptote x=3.

KeyConcepts.Title: Logarithm domain
KeyConcepts.Rule: Strict positivity; zero and negative arguments invalid.

KeyConcepts.Title: Vertical asymptote
KeyConcepts.Definition: A logarithmic graph approaches a vertical boundary where its argument tends zero from the positive side.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Solve u(x)=0, then check valid approach direction.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph transformations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Log graph transforms by shifts, stretches and reflections.
KeyConcepts.Rule: x−h moves right; x+h moves left; negative multiplier reflects across x-axis.
